name: Ashveil Cross
summary: The only sanctioned crossing of the Quiet. Where the King's Road meets the scar, a garrison town of silence-bells and veiled lanterns holds the road open — barely. Everyone here is paid to be near the wound, and everyone has a reason they can't leave.
role: garrison and toll town; the Quiet's crossing

ruler.title: Warden of the Cross
ruler.current: Warden Otta Kell, appointed jointly by the Reeve's court and the Censer
ruler.note: The dual appointment means two paymasters, two sets of orders, and one very careful woman.

districts.name: The Veiled Gate
districts.description: The crossing itself: a mile of paved road through the Quiet's edge, lined with silence-bells that ring soundlessly when the scar stirs. Crossed by caravan only at dawn, in single file, with veils drawn.

districts.name: Bellrow
districts.description: The garrison's homes: low stone houses whose doorways face away from the Quiet. Custom forbids looking at the scar after dark.

districts.name: The Toll Market
districts.description: Where caravans pay passage and buy ash-glass trinkets sold as protective charms. Half the charms are fake; the other half are worse.

districts.name: The Ash Cloister
districts.description: A walled Censer outpost where circle-tests are administered to every traveler who cannot produce clean papers.

landmarks.name: The Silence-Bells
landmarks.description: Forty-one bronze bells along the crossing, cast from melted Concord coin. They hang motionless — until the Quiet moves, when they swing without sound. Warden Kell's private tally of silent-rings is the continent's best data on the scar's growth.

landmarks.name: The Last Well
landmarks.description: The town's only sweet-water well, dug deep past the ash-line. Its water tastes faintly of metal, and locals say dreams drunk here are true.

landmarks.name: Kell's Tally-House
landmarks.description: The warden's office, where forty-one years of bell-records are kept in sealed tubes. The Veil-Wardens would trade much for copies; the Censer forbids their release.

conflicts: Two masters: the Reeve's court funds the road, the Censer funds the cloister, and Warden Kell serves both badly.
The Quiet advanced a hand's width this year — the Veiled Gate will need re-paving within a decade, or abandoning.
Smugglers use dawn-crossings to move banned texts between the Hollow Mile and the Burning Sands' Rememberers.
Refugees from dying ash-farms crowd the road north; the town has neither food nor legal grounds to turn them away.

inhabitants.note: Garrison families, toll-keepers, and ash-farmers who won't leave.
Stone-wardens who maintain the crossing's pavement; they volunteer for work no one else will take.
Caravan hands on the southern routes; they cross the Quiet with unsettling calm.
Verdant kin come only to read the ash-line's progress. They never stay the night.
